Every number/definition traces to a page fetched this run (URL + retrieved 2026-08-29 in sources frontmatter); action-first Quick Answers, FAQ shortcodes kept (3 each), hero_below_answer: true, slugs/dates/authors preserved, updated set to 2026-08-29. findings: PAST-DUE: CFPB's guidance page (consumerfinance.gov/housing/housing-insecurity/help-for-renters/get-help-paying-rent-and-bills/, fetched via curl+browser-UA after web_fetch 403'd) carries verbatim: 'Get year-round help with utility bills by contacting your local Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) office or calling the National Energy Assistance Referral Hotline at (866)-674-6327', plus 211 for locating options. liheap.org (fetched) verifies 'roughly 6.7 million households' and block-grants-to-local-agencies targeting shutoff prevention.

PAST-DUE: Two named-state notice frameworks verified from primary law — MN 216B.096 (public utilities; Oct 1–Apr 30 cold-weather moratorium for ≤50% state-median-income households on payment agreements; 10 working days mail / 7 personal notice; no Friday/weekend/holiday disconnection; appeal to commission bars disconnection, 20-working-day decision) and MN 216B.097 (municipal/cooperatives; same window; ≥30 days after mailed / 15 days after personally delivered notice). TX adds the 10-day written-notice period, disputed-charges disconnection bar, and energy-assistance-payment protection (puc.texas.gov Know Your Rights, fetched).

DEPOSIT: The wave-1 TX pattern verified on PUCT's own consumer site: 'The amount of the deposit may be up to 1/5th of the estimated annual billing or the sum of the estimated billings for the next two months' plus disconnection-for-deposit-nonpayment (puc.texas.gov/consumer-help/faq/electricity/, fetched). CA side verified via SCE Help Center: 'currently not billing deposits for residential customers'; if resumed, 2× average monthly billing over last 12 months; refund mailed with closing bill within 30 days, auto-applied 10 days after final shutoff; review after 12 consecutive on-time bills. MN 216B.098 verified: no additional deposit for customers current under an accepted payment agreement.

DEPOSIT — honest scope line: interest-on-deposit and the specific 65+/disability waiver language from the wave-1 pattern were NOT verified this run (Texas Administrative Code §25.496 gated 401/redirect to JS portal; SCE's 'avoid paying deposit' page bot-walled; MN 216B.025 returned no statute text). Per mission constraints, nothing unverifiable was installed; those elements are marked for a future run rather than fabricated.

ESTIMATED: ConEd's bill FAQ (fetched; content client-rendered and recovered via reader proxy of the live URL) gives verbatim: higher-bill factors including 'More days in the billing period', 'Whether the current or previous bills were estimated', and supply-price fluctuation ('We pass our costs on to you without making a profit'); the 13-month usage bar chart; photo-of-meter + upload workflow; 'If you were billed for more energy than you used, we will credit your account right away.' ConEd's how-to-read-your-meter page verified live. PUCT FAQ verified: estimates allowed only when reads can't be obtained, max three consecutive billing cycles; Know-Your-Rights verified: no disconnection for an estimated bill outside defined exceptions.

Internal-link spec met: 21 → how-to-dispute, 28-reconnection, can-utility-shut-off-service (hub), 26 (4 links); 26 → hub, 21, 28 (3 links); 14 → how-to-dispute, 21, 18-fuel, 16-budget-billing, hub, 26 (6 links).
